description: The bar chart illustrates the accuracy performance (in percentage) of different models on a multimodal audio reasoning benchmark, comparing two input modalities — “Audio” (blue bars) and “Noise” (purple bars) — alongside a baseline “Random Choice” (dashed gray line) set at approximately 30% accuracy. The horizontal axis categorizes three model configurations: an unlabeled gray bar (likely a placeholder or control), “Audio-Reasoner,” and “Qwen-2.5-Omni.” For the “Audio-Reasoner,” the Audio modality achieves ~37% accuracy while Noise reaches ~30%; for “Qwen-2.5-Omni,” Audio significantly outperforms Noise, with ~57% versus ~36% accuracy. The Random Choice baseline remains constant across categories, visually underscoring that both models perform above chance, particularly Qwen-2.5-Omni on Audio, which nearly doubles the baseline. The vertical axis ranges from 0 to 60% in increments of 10, and the legend clearly distinguishes the three conditions using color and line style. The chart visually emphasizes the superiority of audio input over noise input, especially for the more advanced Qwen-2.5-Omni model, aligning with the paper’s focus on deep reasoning in audio modalities.
